# Conformance matrix

<!-- Generated by conformance/report.py from conformance/results/. Do not edit. -->

How 27 parser runs treat the same files in JSON5, JSONC, JWCC (HuJSON), JSON
Lines and strict JSON. Each dialect's table lists the parsers that claim that dialect.
Run on 2026-10-28; a full run took 14 s. How it works and how to
rerun it: [conformance/README.md](../conformance/README.md).

Cells: ✓ the parser agrees with the expected verdict, ✗ it disagrees, 💥 it crashed or
took longer than 10 s. Where the spec allows both verdicts (expected: either), the cell
shows what the parser did: A accepted, R rejected. Duplicate keys count as valid in the
syntax tables (jsonvet runs with `--ignore duplicate-key`); they have their own table.

Expected verdicts come from the spec where it decides the case (marked †, with the section
under the table), from the json5-tests file extension, from conformance/extra/, or else
from jsonvet's reviewed corpus snapshot. Where jsonvet disagrees with a spec, its column
shows ✗ like any other parser.

Spec notes (†):

- [corpus/json5/bom.json](../tests/corpus/json5/bom.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §8: U+FEFF is white space.
- [corpus/json5/combining-mark-in-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/combining-mark-in-key.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §3 and ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6: a combining mark may continue a key.
- [corpus/json5/escape-letter.json](../tests/corpus/json5/escape-letter.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §5.1: an unknown escape keeps the letter and drops the backslash.
- [corpus/json5/escaped-newline-in-string.json](../tests/corpus/json5/escaped-newline-in-string.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §5.1: a backslash before a line break continues it.
- [corpus/json5/hex-and-friends.json](../tests/corpus/json5/hex-and-friends.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §6: hex, bare decimal points, plus signs, Infinity, NaN.
- [corpus/json5/letter-u0e33-starts-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/letter-u0e33-starts-key.json): ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6: U+0E33 is a letter in every Unicode version.
- [corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028-clean.json](../tests/corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028-clean.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §7: a line comment ends at a LineTerminator, and U+2028 is one.
- [corpus/json5/negative-hex.json](../tests/corpus/json5/negative-hex.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §6: hex numbers may be signed.
- [corpus/json5/raw-u2028-in-string.json](../tests/corpus/json5/raw-u2028-in-string.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §5.2: U+2028 may appear raw in a string (the grammar in §9.1 says otherwise).
- [corpus/json5/top-level-scalar.json](../tests/corpus/json5/top-level-scalar.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §2: a JSON5 text is any value.
- [corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key-escaped.json](../tests/corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key-escaped.json): ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6: an escape in a key must still be a character allowed there.
- [corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §3 and ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6: a combining mark cannot start a key.
- [corpus/json5/double-comma-array.json](../tests/corpus/json5/double-comma-array.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §4: a single comma may follow the final element.
- [corpus/json5/empty.json](../tests/corpus/json5/empty.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §9.2: a JSON5 text is exactly one value.
- [corpus/json5/escape-nine.json](../tests/corpus/json5/escape-nine.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §9.1: escapes of the digits 1 to 9 are not in the grammar.
- [corpus/json5/key-with-dash.json](../tests/corpus/json5/key-with-dash.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §3: an unquoted key must be an IdentifierName.
- [corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028.json](../tests/corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §7: the comment ends at U+2028, so x is left over.
- [corpus/json5/lone-comma-array.json](../tests/corpus/json5/lone-comma-array.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §4: a single comma may follow the final element.
- [corpus/json5/lone-comma-object.json](../tests/corpus/json5/lone-comma-object.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §3: a single comma may follow the final member.
- [corpus/json5/number-led-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/number-led-key.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §3: an unquoted key must be an IdentifierName.
- [corpus/json5/punctuation-u00b7-in-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/punctuation-u00b7-in-key.json): ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6: U+00B7 is punctuation, not allowed in a key (ECMAScript 2015 later allowed it).
- [corpus/json5/raw-newline-in-string.json](../tests/corpus/json5/raw-newline-in-string.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §5: a string cannot hold a raw line break.
- [corpus/json5/unclosed-comment-own-star-slash.json](../tests/corpus/json5/unclosed-comment-own-star-slash.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §7: the */ cannot reuse the opening *.
- [corpus/json5/unclosed-comment.json](../tests/corpus/json5/unclosed-comment.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §7: a block comment ends with */.
- [corpus/json5/whitespace-only.json](../tests/corpus/json5/whitespace-only.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §9.2: a JSON5 text is exactly one value.
- [corpus/json5/depth-10000.json](../tests/corpus/json5/depth-10000.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §10: a parser may limit the depth of nesting.
- [corpus/json5/depth-10001.json](../tests/corpus/json5/depth-10001.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §10: a parser may limit the depth of nesting.
- [corpus/json5/integer-5000-digits.json](../tests/corpus/json5/integer-5000-digits.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §10: a parser may limit the range of numbers.
- [corpus/json5/mark-u1885-starts-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/mark-u1885-starts-key.json): ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6 allows any Unicode version from 3.0: U+1885 was a letter until Unicode 9.0, a mark since.
- [corpus/json5/not-utf8.json](../tests/corpus/json5/not-utf8.json): JSON5 1.0.0 §9.1 works on Unicode characters and names no byte encoding.

Notable disagreements:

- [corpus/json5/bom.json](../tests/corpus/json5/bom.json): Go `titanous/json5` rejects a leading byte order mark, which §8 lists as white space.
- [corpus/json5/escape-letter.json](../tests/corpus/json5/escape-letter.json): Go `titanous/json5` rejects `\a`, which §5.1 says is a plain `a`.
- [corpus/json5/hex-and-friends.json](../tests/corpus/json5/hex-and-friends.json): Go `titanous/json5` rejects `-NaN`, and Rust `serde_json5` rejects `+Infinity`; §6 allows a sign on both.
- [corpus/json5/letter-u0e33-starts-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/letter-u0e33-starts-key.json): Go `titanous/json5` takes only ASCII letters, digits, `_` and `$` in unquoted keys, with no escapes, so it also rejects the keys in other rows that hold accents, combining marks or `\u` escapes.
- [corpus/json5/negative-hex.json](../tests/corpus/json5/negative-hex.json): Rust `serde_json5` rejects a sign on a hex number, `-0x10` and `+0x1F` alike.
- [corpus/json5/raw-u2028-in-string.json](../tests/corpus/json5/raw-u2028-in-string.json): Rust `serde_json5` rejects a raw U+2028 in a string. §5.2 allows it but the grammar in §9.1 does not, so the spec shares the blame.
- [corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key-escaped.json](../tests/corpus/json5/combining-mark-starts-key-escaped.json): Python `json5`, `pyjson5` and Rust `serde_json5` accept an escaped combining mark at the start of a key; ECMAScript 5.1 §7.6 does not allow one there.
- [corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028.json](../tests/corpus/json5/line-comment-ends-at-u2028.json): Go `titanous/json5` does not end a line comment at U+2028, so the stray `x` after it disappears into the comment.
- [corpus/json5/punctuation-u00b7-in-key.json](../tests/corpus/json5/punctuation-u00b7-in-key.json): Rust `serde_json5` accepts a middle dot (U+00B7) in a key. ECMAScript 2015 allows it; ECMAScript 5.1, which JSON5 cites, does not.
- [corpus/json5/unclosed-comment.json](../tests/corpus/json5/unclosed-comment.json): Go `titanous/json5` accepts a block comment that never closes at the end of the file (also unclosed-comment-own-star-slash.json and json5-tests unterminated-block-comment.txt).
- [corpus/json5/depth-10000.json](../tests/corpus/json5/depth-10000.json): Python `json5` raises RecursionError. Rust `serde_json5` overflowed its stack in the 2026-10-14 run and parsed the file in the 2026-10-19 run, with the same version, compiler and 8 MB stack, so its verdict here is not stable. `pyjson5` rejects the file at its own nesting limit, which §10 allows.

Spec notes (†):

- [extra/jsonc/line-comment-at-end.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/line-comment-at-end.jsonc): Syntax, single-line comments: a line comment may run to the end of the file.
- [extra/jsonc/lone-cr-ends-comment.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/lone-cr-ends-comment.jsonc): Conventions: a lone CR is a line ending, so it ends a line comment.
- [extra/jsonc/block-comment-unclosed.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/block-comment-unclosed.jsonc): Syntax, multi-line comments: a block comment ends with */.
- [extra/jsonc/comment-only.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/comment-only.jsonc): Comments sit where JSON allows whitespace; JSON needs a value.
- [extra/jsonc/hash-comment.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/hash-comment.jsonc): Appendix B: comments that start with # are not supported.
- [extra/jsonc/json5-syntax.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/json5-syntax.jsonc): Beyond JSON, JSONC adds only comments (and optional trailing commas): no unquoted keys, single quotes or hex.
- [extra/jsonc/nested-block-comment.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/nested-block-comment.jsonc): Syntax, multi-line comments: they cannot nest, so the first */ ends the comment.
- [corpus/jsonc/line-comment-not-ended-by-u2028.json](../tests/corpus/jsonc/line-comment-not-ended-by-u2028.json): JSONC, Conventions: a line ending is LF, CRLF or CR, so U+2028 does not end the comment.
- [extra/jsonc/trailing-comma-array.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/trailing-comma-array.jsonc): Syntax, trailing commas: parsers MAY support them.
- [corpus/jsonc/trailing-comma.json](../tests/corpus/jsonc/trailing-comma.json): JSONC, Trailing commas: parsers MAY support them.

Notable disagreements:

- [extra/jsonc/lone-cr-ends-comment.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/lone-cr-ends-comment.jsonc): `strip-json-comments` and Go `tidwall/jsonc` end a line comment only at LF, so a comment ended by a lone CR swallows the rest of the file.
- [extra/jsonc/comment-only.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/comment-only.jsonc): The Rust `jsonc-parser` returns no value and no error for a file holding only a comment; the driver counts that as an accept.
- [extra/jsonc/json5-syntax.jsonc](../conformance/extra/jsonc/json5-syntax.jsonc): The Rust `jsonc-parser` accepts unquoted keys, single quotes and hex by default; it is lenient by design.

- [extra/jwcc/two-trailing-commas.json](../conformance/extra/jwcc/two-trailing-commas.json): Only one comma may follow the final element.
- [extra/jwcc/unquoted-key.json](../conformance/extra/jwcc/unquoted-key.json): Unquoted strings are not part of JWCC.
- [corpus/jwcc/single-quotes.json](../tests/corpus/jwcc/single-quotes.json): JWCC adds only comments and trailing commas; no single quotes.
- [extra/jwcc/u2028-in-line-comment.json](../conformance/extra/jwcc/u2028-in-line-comment.json): Only \n ends a line comment, so b is comment text; but JWCC is meant to be valid JavaScript, where U+2028 ends it.

Notable disagreements:

- [extra/jwcc/line-comment-at-end.json](../conformance/extra/jwcc/line-comment-at-end.json): `hujson`, the reference implementation, rejects a line comment that ends the file without a newline. The spec allows that since its 2021-07-20 update (reported as tailscale/hujson#56).

Spec notes (†):

- [extra/jsonl/crlf.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/crlf.jsonl): Rule 3: \r\n works because whitespace around a value is ignored.
- [extra/jsonl/padded-line.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/padded-line.jsonl): Rule 3: whitespace around a value is ignored.
- [extra/jsonl/scalars.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/scalars.jsonl): Rule 2: any JSON value is permitted on a line.
- [corpus/jsonl/crlf-duplicate.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/crlf-duplicate.jsonl): JSON Lines rule 3: \r\n works, as white space around a value.
- [corpus/jsonl/no-final-newline.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/no-final-newline.jsonl): JSON Lines rule 3: a final line terminator is not required.
- [extra/jsonl/bom.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/bom.jsonl): Rule 1: a byte order mark must NOT be included.
- [extra/jsonl/trailing-blank-line.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/trailing-blank-line.jsonl): Rule 3: a final line terminator must be the last byte of the file.
- [corpus/jsonl/blank-line.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/blank-line.jsonl): JSON Lines rule 2: a blank line is not a value.
- [corpus/jsonl/two-values-on-a-line.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/two-values-on-a-line.jsonl): JSON Lines rule 2: each line is one JSON value.
- [corpus/jsonl/value-across-lines.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/value-across-lines.jsonl): JSON Lines rule 2: each line is one JSON value.

Notable disagreements:

- [extra/jsonl/scalars.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/scalars.jsonl): Python `jsonlines` rejects a `null` line unless you pass `allow_none=True`; the spec permits any JSON value.
- [extra/jsonl/bom.jsonl](../conformance/extra/jsonl/bom.jsonl): Python `jsonlines` accepts a leading byte order mark, which the spec forbids.
- [corpus/jsonl/blank-line.jsonl](../tests/corpus/jsonl/blank-line.jsonl): Go's `json.Decoder` and serde_json's `StreamDeserializer` read values split by any white space, not by lines. They are how those languages usually read JSON Lines, so blank lines, two values on a line and a value across lines all pass.

Spec notes (†):

- [corpus/i-json/duplicate-key.json](../tests/corpus/i-json/duplicate-key.json): RFC 8259 §4: names SHOULD be unique, but repeats are valid syntax.
- [corpus/i-json/lone-surrogate.json](../tests/corpus/i-json/lone-surrogate.json): RFC 8259 §8.2: the grammar allows a lone surrogate escape.
- [corpus/i-json/unsafe-integer.json](../tests/corpus/i-json/unsafe-integer.json): RFC 8259 §6: the grammar has no range limit (I-JSON has one).
- [corpus/json/duplicate-key.json](../tests/corpus/json/duplicate-key.json): RFC 8259 §4: names SHOULD be unique, but repeats are valid syntax.
- [corpus/json/lone-surrogates-are-distinct-keys.json](../tests/corpus/json/lone-surrogates-are-distinct-keys.json): RFC 8259 §8.2: the grammar allows lone surrogates.
- [corpus/json/leading-zero.json](../tests/corpus/json/leading-zero.json): RFC 8259 §6: a number cannot have a leading zero.
- [json5-tests/comments/irregular-block-comment.json](../tests/json5-tests/comments/irregular-block-comment.json): json5/json5-tests#4: named .json but has a block comment, so it is not JSON.
- [corpus/i-json/bom.json](../tests/corpus/i-json/bom.json): RFC 8259 §8.1: a parser MAY ignore a byte order mark.
- [corpus/json/bom.json](../tests/corpus/json/bom.json): RFC 8259 §8.1: a parser MAY ignore a byte order mark.

Notable disagreements:

- [corpus/i-json/lone-surrogate.json](../tests/corpus/i-json/lone-surrogate.json): serde_json rejects an escaped lone surrogate when it builds the string, though the RFC 8259 grammar allows one (§8.2).
- [corpus/json/nan-and-infinity.json](../tests/corpus/json/nan-and-infinity.json): Python's `json` accepts NaN, Infinity and -Infinity by default; RFC 8259 §6 has no such numbers.

## Duplicate keys

Every spec here lets a parser keep one of the values, and JSON5 §3 also lets it fail. Only four
parsers in the matrix can report duplicates: Python's `json` through an `object_pairs_hook`
that raises, Python `json5` with `allow_duplicate_keys=False`, jiter with
`catch_duplicate_keys=True`, and jsonvet by default. The
others have no switch for it in their sources, and accepted these files wherever their syntax
allowed. A dash means the parser rejects the file's syntax, so the test says nothing.
